html:
A Tagalog poet of the Spanish era in the Philippines, author of Florante at Laura, which is counted among the founding works of Filipino literature.

He was born in Bulacan, studied in Manila while working as a house servant, and learned verse from older Tagalog poets. Florante at Laura, published around 1838, is a long poem in the awit form. It is set in a far off Albania, where a hero fights tyranny, treachery and a false ruler. Many readers then and since have seen it as a hidden protest against Spanish colonial rule, written when open criticism was dangerous. Balagtas spent time in prison, later lived in Bataan, and took the surname Baltazar after an 1849 decree on Filipino surnames.

His poem was read and memorised by later generations. José Rizal carried a copy, and Apolinario Mabini copied it by hand. In Filipino, a poetic debate is still called a balagtasan in his honour. He wrote at the same time as the great poets of mainland Southeast Asia, such as Sunthorn Phu of Siam and Nguyễn Du of Vietnam.
sum: A Tagalog poet of the Spanish era in the Philippines, author of Florante at Laura, which is counted among the founding works of Filipino literature.
